title: Paid Media in Miami: Google, Meta, TikTok Ads | 22 Signals
description: Paid media for Miami companies: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads in English and Spanish, creative made in-house, and every lead tracked to revenue.
eyebrow: Paid Media in Miami (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok ads)
h1: Paid media for Miami brands: Google, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok ads that pay back
intro: We run paid media for established Miami companies across Google Search, Performance Max, YouTube, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok. Campaigns run in English and Spanish, creative is made by our own video and design team, and every call, form and booking is tracked into your CRM. Developers, clinics, hotels and brands see which ads bring revenue, not just clicks.

sections.h: The problem: spend going out, no idea what comes back
p: Many Miami companies spend real money on ads and still cannot answer a simple question: which campaign brought in last month's best customers? The agency reports clicks and cost per lead. Sales says the leads are poor. Nobody connects the two, and the Spanish campaigns are a copy of the English ones with the words swapped.

Good paid media Miami companies can trust starts at the other end: what a good customer is worth, how they buy, and which language they buy in. Then we build campaigns, landing pages and tracking around that, so every dollar can be traced to an outcome. If a campaign cannot show revenue after a fair test, we say so and move the budget.

YouTube and Meta campaigns for awareness and retargeting
LinkedIn campaigns for B2B buyers in finance, trade and professional services
TikTok campaigns for fashion, beauty and hospitality brands
Creative made in-house: video, motion graphics, static and carousel ads
Landing pages written and built for each campaign and language

sections.h: Rules that shape ads in Miami's biggest sectors
p: Several of Miami's main industries come with advertising restrictions that trip up generic agencies. Getting these right protects your accounts from being suspended. The problems that most often hide in ad accounts are rejected ads nobody noticed, landing pages that break policy, and audiences the platform no longer allows. For paid media Miami brands run in these sectors, a policy review comes before any new spend.
list: Real estate: Meta treats housing ads as a special category with limited targeting by age, gender and ZIP code, so campaigns rely on creative and broad audiences instead
Healthcare and aesthetics: Google and Meta both restrict health claims, before-and-after images and targeting based on health conditions, so ads and landing pages are written with that in mind
Crypto and fintech: Google and Meta require advertiser approval or certification for many crypto and financial products, and we plan for that before launch
Hospitality: campaigns timed around winter high season, Art Basel week, Miami Music Week and other event dates when prices and demand shift
Trade and logistics: LinkedIn and Google Search aimed at importers and procurement teams in Latin America, often in Spanish
Fashion and beauty: TikTok and Meta creative that feels native to the feed, tested in short cycles

p: A Miami campaign often needs at least two languages and several countries. A Brickell developer may sell to buyers in Colombia, Argentina, Mexico and Brazil as much as to Floridians. A clinic in Coral Gables may treat patients flying in from across Latin America.

We build separate campaigns by language and market, with their own keywords, ad copy and landing pages, so budget and results are clear for each. Spanish copy is written for the audience, not translated line by line, and the follow-up email or WhatsApp message arrives in the same language as the ad.

sections.h: How it works: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we ask what a good customer is worth, how they buy and what has and has not worked before.
Plan: channel mix, budget split, audiences, creative and tracking plan, with launch dates in writing.
Build: tracking first, then landing pages, creative and campaigns, all checked before a dollar is spent.
Grow: weekly optimization, new creative tests, and a monthly review of spend against revenue.

We set up conversion tracking with consent banners and server-side events where it makes sense, so data stays accurate as browsers block more tracking. Phone calls are tracked too, which matters for clinics and service firms that still book by phone.

If campaigns lead to text messages or automated calls, Florida's Telephone Solicitation Act adds consent rules. We build clear consent into forms and keep records, and leave legal sign-off to your counsel.

We wrote the business, operating and marketing plan to take a US neurotech device to market: who buys, what they need to hear, which channels to use first and how to measure it. Paid media works best when it follows a plan like that, rather than starting with a budget and hoping.

We run our paid media Miami accounts against a written plan. Campaigns are checked and adjusted on a set schedule, and reviews are booked around your team's calendar. Your Signal Lead owns the account and the monthly report.
Because our creative team sits inside the same company, new ads do not wait on a separate agency. When a shoot in Miami is needed, we plan it when the project needs it.
The cost of paid media, Miami or anywhere else, has two parts: your ad spend, paid directly to the platforms, and our management fee, which depends on:

faqs.q: Should Miami businesses run ads in Spanish?
faqs.a: If a meaningful share of your customers speaks Spanish, yes. Spanish speakers search and scroll differently, and an English ad shown to them is easy to ignore. We run them as separate campaigns with their own copy and landing pages, so you can see what each language brings in.

faqs.q: Can you advertise a Miami condo project to buyers in Latin America?
faqs.a: Yes. We target the countries your buyers come from with Google, Meta and YouTube campaigns in Spanish and Portuguese, following Meta's housing ad rules. Ads lead to landing pages in the buyer's language, and inquiries are routed to the right sales agent with the source tracked.

faqs.q: Can med spas and clinics advertise on Meta and Google?
faqs.a: Yes, within each platform's health policies. We avoid restricted claims and targeting, use compliant imagery, and send people to landing pages that meet the same standards. Getting this right keeps ad accounts healthy, which matters more than any single campaign.

faqs.q: Which platform works best for a Brickell fintech or finance firm?
faqs.a: Usually LinkedIn and Google Search for B2B, with Meta and YouTube for consumer products. Many crypto and financial products need advertiser approval first, which we plan before launch. We start with the channel closest to buying intent and expand once tracking shows what works.

faqs.q: Do you work with Miami companies in person?
faqs.a: When it helps, yes. Most paid media work happens inside the ad platforms, so it runs well on calls and shared reports. When we need a photo or video shoot on site in Miami, we plan it when the project needs it and agree dates in writing.

faqs.q: Is there a minimum ad budget?
faqs.a: We do not set a fixed minimum, but the budget needs to be large enough for each campaign to learn and produce results you can judge. We recommend a starting budget for each platform during planning, based on your market and goals, and explain the reasoning.
